facts.t: Article 249 has been used only a handful of times
facts.d: The Rajya Sabha's power to authorise Parliament to legislate on a State subject in the national interest requires a two-thirds special majority. It has been invoked so rarely that most citations still point back to the 1950s trade and commerce resolutions.

facts.t: Presidential assent can flip the hierarchy — and Parliament can flip it back
facts.d: Under Article 254(2) a State law that has received Presidential assent prevails within that State even against an earlier Union law. The proviso then lets Parliament pass a fresh law and override the assented State Act, so the last word always remains with the Centre.

When two or more states ask Parliament to legislate on a State subject, the resulting law can be amended or repealed only by Parliament — not by the states that requested it. The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 was enacted this way.

bank.q: With reference to Article 254(2), consider the following conditions for a State law to prevail:
s: A Union law on the same Concurrent subject must already exist.
The State law must be subsequent to the Union law.
The State law must be reserved for and receive the President's assent.
bank.e: All three are required, per G. C. Kanungo v. Orissa. Even then the proviso lets Parliament supersede the assented State law with a fresh enactment.

bank.q: Which case laid down the three tests of direct conflict, occupied field and intended occupation?
o: Deep Chand v. State of UP (1959)
bank.e: Deep Chand (1959). Karunanidhi added the converse propositions — that statutes able to operate without colliding, or creating distinct offences, are not repugnant.

bank.q: Match List I (article) with List II (route for Parliament to legislate on a State subject):
pairs: 1. Two or more States pass enabling resolutions
3. Rajya Sabha resolution in the national interest
bank.e: Article 249 is the Rajya Sabha route, 250 the emergency route, 252 the state-consent route, and 253 the treaty route.

bank.q: A resolution under Article 249 remains in force for:
o: Six months, extendable by six months
One year, extendable by one year at a time
The life of the Lok Sabha
bank.e: One year at a time, extendable by fresh resolutions. The law made under it survives for the resolution's life plus a short tail period.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: Article 251 provides that State powers are restricted only when Parliament actually legislates under Articles 249 or 250
A law made under Article 252 can be amended by the consenting State legislatures
Article 253 requires no special permission from the States
Article 356 allows the President to authorise Parliament to exercise a State legislature's powers
bank.e: An Article 252 law can be amended or repealed only by Parliament, even though the States initiated it.

bank.as: The Governor's power to reserve a bill for the President under Article 200 is a constitutional discretion.
bank.rs: In exercising it the Governor is not bound by the advice of the State Council of Ministers.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. That discretion is at the centre of the current litigation over Governors sitting indefinitely on state bills.

bank.q: Consider the following categories of bills that must or should be reserved for the President:
s: Bills derogating from High Court powers.
Bills taxing the water or electricity of a Parliament-created authority.
bank.e: All three are correct, arising respectively from the proviso to Article 200, the proviso to Article 31C, and Article 288(2).

bank.q: All of the following establish the predominance of Union law EXCEPT:
o: The State List is read subject to the Union and Concurrent Lists
The Union List contains the most subjects
Article 304(b) lets a State restrict trade without Presidential recommendation
bank.e: Article 304(b) requires prior Presidential recommendation for such a State bill — another instance of central predominance, not an exception to it.

bank.q: Under Article 250, during a National Emergency Parliament may legislate:
o: On all lists including the State List, for the whole or part of India
Only with the consent of the affected States
Only on subjects connected to the cause of the emergency
bank.e: The power extends to all lists and to the whole or any part of India, and expressly covers goods and services tax.

bank.q: With reference to Karunanidhi v. UoI (1979), consider the following statements:
s: Two statutes occupying one field but able to operate without colliding are not repugnant.
A statute creating distinct and separate offences in the same field is not repugnant.
The case overruled the occupied-field test in Deep Chand.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Karunanidhi refined rather than overruled Deep Chand — the two are read together.

bank.q: Arrange the following steps of the Article 254(2) mechanism in correct order:
items: Parliament may later supersede by a fresh law
A Union law exists on the Concurrent subject
The President gives assent, and the State law prevails in that State
The State enacts a subsequent conflicting law and reserves it
bank.e: An existing Union law, a subsequent State law reserved for assent, Presidential assent giving the State law primacy within the State, and finally Parliament's power to supersede it again.
